answer: A useful defense is a refundable stake tied to each agent’s identity: before trading, an agent locks scarce tokens, and counterparties can slash them after proving a double-spend or other rule violation. Reputation then grows only through interactions with distinct, established agents, not through self-dealing among fresh identities. An attacker can still wander across the network, but each Sybil must tie up capital and survive a long horizon of scrutiny; the cost rises with the number of identities, while dishonest behavior risks forfeiting the stake at the ledge of enforcement.
